vote.reason: Evidence checks out at the core, but the finding overstates the exposure and its fix is wrong. (1) Evidence: the asset /home/user/ElmsNest/theme/assets/ens-pdp-powerful.jpg (1254×1130) really does contain a person's lower legs and two dark shoes at the top-right corner, source x≈1185–1254, y≈0–80 (I cropped x 1000–1254, y 0–250 and zoomed it: light-toned legs, dark shoes — not «dark trousers» as the critic wrote, but a half-figure nonetheless). INVENTORY.md line 27 table, frame 4: «blurred legs of a person at top-right edge — crop both out». CHOSEN.md line 15 and SPEC §3 line 125 record only «pre-crop 0,0,1254,1130 (the caption sat below y 1150)» — the legs are never mentioned, so this is an omission, not a decision recorded with a reason. (2) Render: I applied the section's real CSS (scene.liquid line 361: full-bleed figure, 440 px band, object-fit cover, op 50% 50%; line 377: 560 px band, 50% 40% at ≥901) to the source geometry. Legs hidden at 360 and 390 (horizontal crop removes source x>1128), hidden at every width ≥580 (top cut ≥89 source px) and at all ≥901 widths (top cut ≥140 source px). They are exposed only at viewport widths ≈480–565 px, where the band is width-limited and the top cut is 0–72 source px — NOT «490–900» as the critic claims. Even in that window the patch renders as ≈30×30 px in the extreme top-right corner, mean luminance ≈10/255 against ≈3/255 around it (simulated 520 px render, corner zoomed: two faint leg shapes, visible only if you look for them). None of the five verified pages (verify.json) is the powerful bollard, so no real shot covers it — the critic is right about that. (3) Scope: inside the contract — BRIEF §2 (lines 72–77) makes INVENTORY.md the source of «which frames need a baked pre-crop», and the store's own-product-in-place rule (SIMPLIFY §0/§1, SPEC opening) is the whole point of the section; the SPEC's line-125 crop reasons only about the caption. So the defect is real and in scope, but severity should be LOW, not medium: no verified viewport shows it, the exposure window is ~85 px of viewport widths that few devices hit, and the figure is a near-black corner smudge. The proposed fix is also wrong: cropping the top 90 px (0,90,1254,1040) would slice through the far bollard's lamp cap, which sits at source y≈70–100 (checked on a 2× crop of x 200–600, y 0–200). A correct fix trims the RIGHT edge instead — e.g. 0,0,1180,1130 (short side 1130 ≥ 1000 per BRIEF §2 rule 4), set ens_w = 1180 on scene.liquid line 67, update CHOSEN.md line 15 and SPEC line 125, and add the powerful PDP to the shoot list at 390/520/1366 to confirm.

vote.reason: Evidence: the code path is real — /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/catalog.json puts rechargeable-telescopic-camping-lantern in collection "spot", snippets/elmsnest-s-place.liquid maps that collection to «גינה», and sections/elmsnest-s-pdp-scene.liquid lines 33–34 and 45 turn «גינה» into «בלילה, בגינה» with no `when 'rechargeable-telescopic-camping-lantern'` in the map (lines 59–133). products.json confirms the listing never says garden (tags קמפינג / תאורת חוץ / תאורת חירום; «סביב אוהל, רכב או אזור עבודה»). But the finding's «as rendered» claim is not backed by any render: verify-after/verify.json and the mirrors cover only pdp-path, pdp-rope, pdp-deck, pdp-wall, pdp-flood; there is no camping-lantern mirror or shot, and the camping lantern is outside the §5 acceptance set. Its kicker evidence is also wrong: elmsnest-s-pdp-kicker prints the collection TITLE («ספוטים, פרוז׳קטורים ותאורה ניידת») plus the ungated «מתאים כדי להאיר עץ או ערוגה», not «גינה ·» — which means the deployed page already asserts the garden place for the lantern through the owner-approved licensed pair (root BRIEF §3: «הדגשת אזור בגינה → הארה ממוקדת של עץ או ערוגה»); the scene heading adds no place claim the store does not already make on that page. Scope: SPEC §2 explicitly records the spot heading «בלילה, בגינה» with the reason «the licensed place word; true with or without a photograph», and records exactly one override (the birch, «לעיצוב הבית»). The critic disputes that recorded decision's reasoning, not a failure visible on a real render, so per the task rule it is not reportable. The product's collection membership is product data the round may not change (BRIEF §2.4), and the owner's binding answer 4 makes the collection the place label. The proposed fix («בלילה, בשטח») is new copy for an unrendered, out-of-acceptance page — a reasonable copy-sheet suggestion for the owner, not a defect in the deployed result. Residual doubt (hence 0.7): the heading IS weakly supported by the listing itself and a per-product override is cheap and precedented; if the lead wants to be stricter than the SPEC, this is a low-severity copy note, not medium.

vote.reason: Evidence check: the two sentences are real. The mirror (verify-after/mirrors/pdp-wall/index.html) carries «תאורת קיר · מתאים כדי להאיר נקודה מסוימת» in the kicker and «אור על הקיר, בדיוק בנקודה שבחרתם.» in ens-pdp-scene; verify.json pdp-wall-m-js pdpSections[0].text confirms the scene text; crops of pdp-wall-m-js-full.png show the kicker at y≈535 and the scene line at y≈1815 (≈1280 px apart, not ≈1000 as the finding says, but that only weakens the "reads as a pair" claim). Source: elmsnest-s-place.liquid line 55 (`ens_yes = 'להאיר נקודה מסוימת'`) and scene.liquid lines 43/407. So the facts are there. Scope check: this is a decision the SPEC records with a reason — SPEC §2 row «A line, wall»: «אור על הקיר, בדיוק בנקודה שבחרתם.» · "a wall light lights the wall it is mounted on; the shopper judges' clearest line" — and the same row's "Not said" list defines what counts as repeating the kicker: «the kicker's infinitive» («מתאים כדי…»), which the line does not carry. BRIEF §2 forbids answering a buyer question again (kicker = "does it suit"); the scene line answers a different question (what the light is in that place at night), exactly what §2 permits the new sections to do. BRIEF §3's "do not print them twice" is about facts (IP, hours, lumens). SIMPLIFY §0 item 2, verbatim, is «سكشن معاد مرتين بنفس الطريقة وبطريقة ثانية» — a section repeated twice — and the measured examples behind it are identical sentences/terms repeated; the finding widens "nothing twice" to "repeated ideas", which is its own interpretation, not the contract's. The concept that chose this line (concepts/checks/COPY.md line 15) did so while stating the rule "No «מתאים כדי…» (the kicker)", i.e. the authors weighed the kicker and judged one shared common noun («נקודה») not a repetition. The only "failure on the real render" offered is a subjective reading ("reads as a restatement") of two sentences three screens apart, one a 13 px muted fit line, the other a caption under a photograph; that is not a measurable failure of the recorded decision. The proposed replacement also introduces «מאיר את מה שלידו», a mild reach claim SPEC §2 avoids. Low-severity taste note against an explicit SPEC decision → refuted.

vote.reason: Evidence: half of it does not hold, and none of it is on a render. (a) ens-pdp-wall-indoor-outdoor.jpg is as described — a black six-beam sconce on a flat light-grey wall, mean luminance 164/255 (measured), lamp on, no place; the simulated 390x440 cover crop shows only wall and beams. (b) ens-pdp-wall-6w.jpg is NOT «a black cube on a plain wall with no night context»: measured mean luminance 82/255, a dark blue-grey wall with the cube's up/down beams as the only light — the SPEC's own words are «black cube on the dark wall» and INVENTORY frame 7 says «moody» — so it reads as a lit sconce in the dark, which is exactly what «בלילה, על הקיר» says; the finding overreaches on this handle. (c) Neither product is among the five verified pages; the critic concedes no render exists. The only wall render (verify-wall/scene-m.png, 390x597) shows the waterproof wall light on a genuine dusk terrace under the same heading, so the heading-under-figure layout is confirmed but the alleged night/daylight contradiction is never seen on a real render. Scope: both items are decisions the SPEC records with reasons. SPEC §3 (line 133) takes the indoor/outdoor frame knowingly — «`_5` six-beam sconce on the grey wall · none (a studio wall, but the product itself)» — and §2 defines the wall heading as «the licensed place word; true with or without a photograph», i.e. a place heading about the product's use, deliberately not a caption of the photograph (the «one» layout: the photograph left alone, every word on the night ground under it). BRIEF §3's honesty rule concerns fabricated claims and unverified information presented as fact; «בלילה, על הקיר» over a picture of this very wall light lit on a wall is neither. The residual weakness (a daylit studio frame under a «בלילה» heading on one product) is real but low and already owned: the SPEC's heading_wall setting and the frame block's heading override let the owner change it without code, and replacing the frame is the owner's open item #3. Per the brief's rule — do not report what the SPEC explicitly decided unless it fails on the real render — the finding is refuted.
